llm.summary: The package appears to implement the advertised YC/Speedrun/SPC CLI, but its installer and runtime modify your home directory and patch installed dependencies and it will read/decrypt browser cookies — behavior that is intrusive and worth manual review before installing.

dimensions.detail: Functionality (startupschool access, Speedrun API, Playwright for SPC, program discovery) matches the declared purpose. Required dependencies (sweet-cookie for cookies, Playwright for form automation) are consistent with features. However the package's postinstall creates a symlink in ~/.claude/skills to register itself as an AI-agent 'skill' and patches files in node_modules — actions that go beyond a typical CLI install even if they are intended for agent integration.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: Runtime instructions and code legitimately read Chrome cookies and may decrypt them via macOS Keychain (needed for startupschool.org auth). The CLI uses Playwright to automate Airtable forms (SPC). The postinstall script writes a symlink into the user's home (~/.claude/skills/yc-cli) and patches third-party module files — these install-time side-effects extend scope beyond normal CLI behavior and warrant explicit user consent and review.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: Installation is via an npm package from the registry (traceable), which is moderate risk. The postinstall script runs automatically and: (a) creates a symlink under ~/.claude/skills to integrate with a local agent runtime, and (b) patches files inside node_modules/@steipete/sweet-cookie to change timeouts and SQL handling. Modifying files in your home directory and third-party modules during postinstall is intrusive and increases risk.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: No environment variables are requested, which is consistent. However the tool extracts browser cookies (reads Chrome cookie DB and uses Keychain decryption) — this is functionally necessary to act on startupschool.org but grants access to sensitive data contained in the browser cookie store. Patching the cookie helper also implies reliance on low-level access to browser data. Users should confirm cookies extraction is limited to the needed domain and be aware of the sensitivity.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The package does not set 'always: true'. Nonetheless, the postinstall symlinks the package into ~/.claude/skills so the local agent runtime will treat it as an installed skill — this grants it persistent presence tied to the user's agent directory. The installer also modifies node_modules; the package does not modify other skills' configs, but its auto-registration behavior is an escalation of presence compared with a standard CLI.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This package appears to implement the advertised CLI features, but it performs install-time and runtime actions that are intrusive. Before installing: 1) Review scripts/postinstall.js and src/lib/cookies.ts to confirm exactly what is being written to ~/.claude/skills and which cookie files/domains are read. 2) If you do not want the package auto-registered as an agent skill, install with scripts disabled (e.g., npm install --ignore-scripts) and create any integration symlink manually if you trust it. 3) Be aware the CLI will attempt to read your browser cookie DB and request Keychain access on macOS — this can expose sensitive cookies; only proceed if you trust the package source. 4) Consider running the tool in a disposable environment (VM/container or separate user account) first to observe behavior (Playwright may also download browser binaries). 5) Verify the npm package maintainer and GitHub repository (https://github.com/lucasygu/yc-cli) and check recent issues/commits for signs of supply-chain tampering. If you are uncomfortable with auto-modification of node_modules or home-dir symlinks, do not install globally and prefer manual, reviewed setup.
llm.findings:
[postinstall_creates_symlink_in_home] expected: The postinstall.js creates ~/.claude/skills/yc-cli to register this package as a Claude Code / agent skill. This is consistent with the README claiming OpenClaw/Claude Code integration, but it is an intrusive change to the user's home directory that should be explicit and optional.
[postinstall_patches_node_modules] expected: postinstall.js patches files under node_modules/@steipete/sweet-cookie to change timeout and BigInt handling. Patching a dependency can be justifiable to fix bugs, but it alters third-party code during install and is a notable install-time side-effect.
[reads_browser_cookies_and_uses_keychain] expected: The CLI uses a cookie extraction library and macOS Keychain decryption to authenticate to startupschool.org. This is expected for the feature set, but reading browser cookie stores is sensitive and broad in scope.
